edit.description: The two clause-only `write_lock` calls (:205, :249) and `author_custom_kind_lock` (:278, called at :342 and :399) declare rows the real writer produces — a `ClauseRow` per clause (`predicate` is a free `String`, so the out-of-vocabulary case still writes: the refusal is on the read side), a `KindFactRow` plus its clause for the custom kind. Route all three through `common::write_lock`. The private raw-TOML `write_lock` (:150) then serves only `drifted_corpus` (:496) and `undeclared_corpus` (:618) — `[[skill]]` rows at UNMATCHABLE_HASH, plus the `layout_import` and `include` families, the first with no field on `drift::Declarations` at all and the second seam-inbound (`drift.rs:3726`: a lock round-trip reads it empty), so `emit` can write neither back and both builders' whole locks stay hand-rendered, the three root clause-row strings their callers concatenate in included (`root_fresh_row` :473, and the inline rows at :657 and :770). Rename the private helper for what it renders so it stops shadowing the common name.

:497's two `[[declaration.kind]]` rows — the built-in `hook` and a `custom_hook` at the same `settings.json#hooks.<Event>` address — are typed `KindFactRow`/`CollectionAddressRow` values; write them through `common::write_lock`. The hand rows declare no `governs` where `common::hook_kind_facts` (tests/it/common/mod.rs:1202) does: spell the rows this case needs rather than bending the fixture to the helper.

:263's `[[declaration.requirement]]` row (inside `check_resolves_the_nested_temper_for_an_explicit_harness_root`) is a `RequirementRow` and `common::write_requirements` (tests/it/common/mod.rs:933) is its home — it merges onto whatever the lock already declares and this fixture declares nothing else. :935's `this is not = = valid toml` stays hand-written: a corrupt lock is a refusal input no writer can emit.

summary: Route the hand-spelled lock fixtures in acceptance, hook_kind and cli through `common::write_lock` — only the drifted-fingerprint and corrupt locks stay hand-rendered.

tests.asserts: `builtin_skill_declared_rows_are_the_whole_contract`, `builtin_skill_out_of_vocabulary_row_is_a_load_error` and the two `author_custom_kind_lock` cases keep their verdicts over a writer-produced lock
`two_kinds_at_the_same_collection_address_trip_collision_loud` still fires exactly one `kind.collection-address-collision` and still pins `rule (0)`
`check_resolves_the_nested_temper_for_an_explicit_harness_root` still fails loud on the unfilled required requirement

acceptance: cargo test green, and the `[[declaration.` grep over the three suites returns only the acceptance.rs drifted-fingerprint family — `drifted_corpus` (:496), `undeclared_corpus` (:618) and the three root clause-row strings their callers hand them (:473, :657, :770) — plus cli.rs:935's corrupt lock. The commit body names every fixture left hand-spelled and why the real writer could not produce it.
